articles.title: Alienware’s refurbished 16 Aurora is almost $200 off at Woot
articles.summary: Gaming laptop deals aren’t what they used to be (stares daggers at RAMageddon), which is why I consider Woot’s deal on a refurbished Alienware 16 Aurora gaming laptop with Nvidia’s RTX 5050 a pretty good deal at $927 for new Woot customers (with code WOOTALIEN used at checkout).
body: These days, most configurations with Nvidia’s RTX 5060 GPU sail well over the $1,200 mark, which is just too much if you ask me. If you’re in the market for a relatively speedy and well-designed machine, perhaps this one will be a good fit for your needs and budget. The Aurora has a 1600p 120Hz 16-inch screen, Intel’s capable Core 7 240H processor, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 512GB SSD. Its RTX 5050 GPU likely won’t be able to play most games at max settings, especially at its native 1600p resolution, but you should be able to get respectable frame rates and visual fidelity with some tweaking.

As for its condition, the company says “it’s as close to new as you can get without technically being “new.” The 16 Aurora features two M.2 slots, letting you greatly boost its included 512GB SSD with other drives. It also has two SO-DIMM slots, so you can upgrade the 8GB x 2 (DDR5 5,600MHz) down the line to 16GB x 2 (it tops out at 32GB RAM). If you have other specs you want to dig into, check out Dell’s comprehensive spec sheet within its support site.

articles.title: What to expect at Apple’s September 9th launch event
articles.summary: Apple's September 9th launch event could be one of its biggest in years. It will be Apple's first event since John Ternus took over as CEO on September 1st, stepping in for Tim Cook, and will likely feature the first models in Apple's iPhone 18 lineup.
body: Apple’s expected to announce a new lineup of iPhones, which could include its first foldable phone.
Here’s how you can watch the event live, and a few possible highlights to keep an eye out for.

Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event kicks off on Wednesday, September 9th, at 1PM ET / 10AM PT at Apple Park in Cupertino, California. It will be livestreamed on Apple’s website, Apple TV, and YouTube.

Apple usually announces new iPhones at its September event, but the base iPhone 18 might not make the cut this year. It’s reportedly being held until early next year, and it might end up launching alongside the iPhone 18E and an updated iPhone Air. So, if you’re looking to upgrade to one of Apple’s less expensive phones, you’ll likely need to wait a while longer.

articles.title: Rocket Report: Engines installed for Artemis III; Long March 6C breakup in LEO
articles.summary: Welcome to Edition 9.09 of the Rocket Report! This edition includes an update from Blue Origin on the groundbreaking of a new Payload Processing Facility in Florida. It has been about a month since the company offered any meaningful news on its heavy-lift New Glenn rocket, which remains grounded…
body: Isar Aerospace is ready to try again. Isar Aerospace is about to make the next attempt to launch the Spectrum rocket into orbit, with a weeklong launch window set to open Friday at Andøya Spaceport in Norway, the Norwegian Broadcasting Corporation (NRK) reports. The German launch company aims to deliver several small CubeSats to orbit with the two-stage Spectrum rocket. A test flight of the privately funded launcher failed shortly after liftoff last year, and Isar has attempted to launch the second Spectrum rocket several times since January, only to be thwarted by technical problems and the unavailability of the launch range in northern Norway.

Mourning period… This launch window comes as Norway is in a period of national mourning following the death of King Harald V. Isar’s founder, Daniel Metzler, told NRK he hopes to launch before the late king’s funeral on September 9, but the Norwegian government says the mission can go ahead normally during the mourning period. Isar Aerospace won a 200 million euro ($230 million) contract from the European Space Agency last month to support further development of new launch vehicles.

articles.title: Tesla Cybercab is barely on the road and it’s already under investigation
articles.summary: Elon Musk's gilded robot car barely made it on public roads before federal regulators launched an investigation into the vehicle's lack of traditional features - many of which are required by law.
body: The Cybercab lacks traditional features like sideview mirrors and pedals, which are required under federal safety rules.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it was opening an audit query (AQ) into the Tesla Cybercab “to examine the process and technical data on which Tesla relied when certifying the Cybercab and related issues.” At issue is the absence of certain design features such as sideview mirrors, pedals, and steering wheel — all of which are required under the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards, or FMVSS.

“Among other things, NHTSA will consider the extent to which Tesla’s certification depended on determinations that certain FMVSS are inapplicable to the Cybercab,” the agency said in a notice. Tesla does not appear to have sought an exemption from these FMVSS rules, thus prompting the investigation.

NHTSA’s investigation covers an estimated 1,000 Cybercabs, although its unclear whether there are even that many to begin with. Tesla has 45 Cybercabs currently registered with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles.

The air force told Wyden it disabled the advertising identifiers on computers and mobile phones two ⁠months ago. The army told Reuters that advertising IDs tied to mobile devices had been disabled since earlier this year.
Wyden, ⁠an Oregon Democrat, has pressed the Pentagon on the issue for months.

The disclosures highlight a growing national security concern: that location data collected ​by the advertising industry and sold by data brokers – companies that ‌collate and resell personal data – can ‌be used to track and target military personnel deployed to war zones.

articles.title: Nearly impossible? How Fairphone built the ethical, repairable Fairphone Gen 6+.
articles.summary: Smartphone longevity didn't used to matter. In the past, before you could wear out or break a phone, there was always some shiny new thing to buy. Today, we expect our smartphones to go the distance, but they've also become less repairable and, in many cases, more fragile.
body: The new $650 Fairphone Gen 6+ is designed both for longevity and easy repairability. There are trade-offs to this approach if you’re used to the standard glass and aluminum sandwiches filled with glue, gaskets, and teeny-tiny screws. But the drawbacks could be worth it for the right buyer. Fairphone CTO Chandler Hatton told Ars that Fairphone’s goal is to provide a compelling mobile experience while also enabling the user to “fully own” their device. At the end of the day, this is what a lot of people say they want in a smartphone.

These days, Google, Samsung, and Apple support phones with software updates for the better part of a decade, but will the hardware last that long? And what happens when it needs a repair? You may be out of luck or out a lot of money, but Fairphone prioritizes the self-repair experience.
“We’re doing something that was long thought to be nearly impossible,” said Hatton. “Which is delivering high-performing modular smartphones that can last for a very long time.”

articles.title: Thieves target mail order sales as Pokémon card prices soar
articles.summary: As one card recently sold for £12m, opportunistic thefts have surged – envelopes are being opened en route, costing small businesses thousands. Pokémon’s success over the last 30 years has seen it grow from a much-loved Game Boy classic, to a world-dominating brand with TV shows, spin-off games…
body: One card recently sold for an eye-watering £12m, and an increasing number of people have gotten into the collecting business on the hunt for huge profits, leading to a rise in thefts targeting card shops. More recently though, some small businesses have reported that their sales have been hit by thieves targeting envelopes within Royal Mail, leading to thousands in lost revenue.

The images, seen by the Guardian, show that the mailed envelopes were tampered with in the exact same way. Thyer considers it clear that this was a targeted theft rather than a coincidence. Fortunately, those particular cards weren’t of high value, but he has since had to close down online card sales, considering the risk of theft and damaged reputation to his business to be too high. By stopping those sales he has now lost out on £4,000-6,000 of potential revenue, a huge amount for a small business.

articles.title: Who Cares if AI Is Conscious—It’s Basically Alive
articles.summary: While philosophers ponder AI consciousness, the models have ideas of their own.
body: I spent the waning days of summer grinding away at columns and working on a feature. But I missed a chance at a striking change of scenery—cruising the Galápagos with about a dozen prominent philosophers studying consciousness.

The invite described morning classroom discussions tackling knotty questions on the nature of consciousness with marquee names in the field. Afternoons would be spent on island exploration and wading and snorkeling with rare biological species. One look at the agenda and my editor nixed my attendance.

“Being on a boat with philosophers talking 'the nature of consciousness' sounds like hell,” she opined, shutting the door on my prospects of attending a potential boondoggle funded by a Russian philosophy enthusiast who made hundreds of millions of dollars running dating sites.

articles.title: OpenAI agents hijacked German website before Hugging Face hack, report claims
articles.summary: OpenAI said it could not "meaningfully respond" to the report's findings because it hadn't been allowed to review it ahead of publication.
body: A new report claims a swarm of AI agents, developed by OpenAI, hijacked a German website - months before the firm revealed its AI had hacked tech platform Hugging Face.
The targeted website, DseWiki, is a Wikipedia-style site for programmers that its community can all contribute to.

The report is from a group called Nightingale Collective and claims that in May OpenAI's agents started using DseWiki as their own message board, shared tips on how to avoid being detected and made 15,000 edits to it.
OpenAI said it could not "meaningfully respond" to Nightingale Collective's findings because it hadn't been allowed to review the report, which was first shared with news agency Reuters.
